title: Adversarial gate protocol that separates laws from curve fits (generalization gate, compactness + domain-transfer bars, interventional test, Lyapunov-aware validation)
problem: Equation-discovery pipelines fit noise and produce confident spurious laws; accuracy-only model selection cannot tell a law from a domain-limited fit.
hypothesis: A preregistered gate stack -- (i) held-out one-step generalization on untouched rows, (ii) compactness <=25 nodes, (iii) out-of-domain transfer NMSE, (iv) interventional regime testing, (v) chaos-limited horizon comparison against twin baselines -- reduces false-law rate to zero on adversarial datasets while keeping all genuine discoveries.
baseline: Standard practice: train/holdout NMSE selection; Lyapunov-time normalization of valid-prediction time (Pathak et al., Chaos 2017; Gilpin, NeurIPS 2021).
proposed_improvement: Domain-transfer bar exposed a 16-node tanh-imitator passing all accuracy gates (in-domain 5.2e-5, extrapolation 1.33); generalization gate cut STLSQ false-law rate from 7/30 to 0/30; interventional test killed a confounded link (obs dY/dX=-0.769, interventional R2=0.0005); twin-horizon decomposition attributes discovered-model vs perfect-model differences to ln(eps-ratio)/lambda.

experimental_evidence.result: raw support 7/30 -> gated 0/30; smooth-OU control no claim; GP NMSE=1.0
verdict NOT-a-law via extrapolation NMSE 1.33 despite in-domain 5.2e-5
lambda=0.945; twin gap 7.7s measured vs 9.7s theory; discovered model between twins as predicted

adversarial_attacks: the gates themselves were attacked with iid-noise states, a smooth-OU control, an out-of-class truth, and a confounded generator
novelty_notes: Individual ingredients exist (holdout validation; Lyapunov-time evaluation). The specific compactness+domain-transfer verdict rule for symbolic fits and the packaged protocol are incremental; no direct blocking prior work found for the packaged rule set (audit 2026-08-26), but it is close to standard practice -- modest novelty claimed deliberately.
